data.long_meaning: Ashcar is a name derived from Sanskrit, which is a combination of the words 'Ash' (god of ash) and 'Car' (chariot). This name carries the spiritual meaning of purification and renewal, as ash is a symbol of transformation and renewal in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ashcar is a powerful and sacred name that represents the divine power of fire. It is believed to bring strength, courage, and wisdom to the one who bears this name. Ashcar is also a symbol of purification, transformation, and illumination.

historical_references.reference: Ashwathama, a great warrior and Pandava ally in the Mahabharata epic, is mentioned as Ashkar in some ancient Indian texts. He is known for his strategic brilliance and unyielding loyalty to his friend Bhishma Pitamaha.

Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, is referred to as Ashkar in inscriptions found in the northwestern regions of India. His empire extended from present-day Afghanistan to Bangladesh around the 3rd century BCE.
